background_notes.fact: For the supplied Fourier Sobolev norms, r>=s implies ||h||_(H^s)<=||h||_(H^r), and ||partial_x h||_(H^s)<=||h||_(H^(s+1)). The multipliers S_t commute with partial_x and Pnz and form a strongly continuous family of isometries on every H^s. Consequently 0<=agamma<1 permits the H^1-to-H^agamma and H^agamma-to-L2 comparisons used here.

background_notes.justification: Compare the nonnegative weights termwise, using <k>>=1 and |k|<=<k>. Fourier multipliers commute. Strong continuity follows by first making the weighted square-sum tail small, uniformly in time by the modulus-one bound, and then using continuity of the finitely many remaining phases. The three cases of agamma satisfy the claimed range.

background_notes.fact: For U,V in H^1(Ttor), partial_x(UV)=(partial_x U)V+U(partial_x V) distributionally, and ||partial_x(UV)||_2<=||UV||_(H^1)<=C||U||_(H^1)||V||_(H^1). If A is in H^(1+gamma) and H^agamma, N007 additionally yields ||partial_x[(S_t A)^2]||_2<=2 C_gamma ||A||_(H^(1+gamma))||A||_(H^agamma). For a continuous Hilbert-space-valued integrand b on [a,b0], its integral satisfies ||integral_a^t b(s)ds||<=integral_a^t||b(s)||ds and has distributional derivative b.

background_notes.justification: Take simultaneous truncations f_m=P_leq(m)f_n and w_m=P_leq(m)w. They are smooth mean-zero states with ||w_m||_(H^gamma)<=M0 and ||f_m-w_m||_2<=delta_n<=1; their distances converge to delta_n. The endpoint Jop formula and its uniform bilinear H^1 bound make F_m converge uniformly on the step in H^1; likewise the comparison stages converge in H^1. BG001 gives convergence in H^agamma and L2. By the H^1 algebra and BG001, Bop_t(F_m,F_m) converges uniformly in L2, so Q_m and then W_m converge in L2, the latter also by N004's sigma=0 continuity. The final projected products converge uniformly in L2 since f_m converges in L2 and F_m converges in H^1 and hence Linfinity. N005's Bop bound gives uniform H^(-pstar) convergence of the derivatives of z_m; together with uniform L2 convergence of z_m this preserves the distributional derivative identity. Strong time continuity needed here follows from BG001 and the bounded bilinear maps. Taking limits preserves each displayed estimate, including its supremum bound. No limiting constant depends on Fourier support.
